entries.s: Result = CreateCamera(#Camera, x, y, Width, Height [, VisibilityMask [, Lod]])
entries.d: Creates a new camera in the current world, at the position x,y with the specified dimensions. Note that these positions and sizes are the position and sizes of the display on the screen, not the position and size of the camera in the world. Unlike other graphics related functions, these coordinates and dimensions are in percents, from 0 to 100 (float numbers can be used for more precise placement). This could seems odd, but 3D applications should be resolution independent and this is a good way of achieving that. If a camera is created with a height of 50% then it will always fill 50% of the height of the screen, irrespective of whether you use a screen which is 640*480 or 1600*1200. If a camera has already been created with the same number, the previous camera is automatically freed and replaced by the new one. Cameras can be overlapped. This means that it is possible to display a camera which fills the whole screen and put a little camera inside which shows another place in the world. To achieve this, the order of creation is very important: the camera which will be on top should be created last.
entries.r: Returns zero if the camera can't be created. If #PB_Any is used as '#Camera' parameter, the new camera number will be returned as 'Result'.

entries.d: Finish the current FastCGI request and free all resources associated to it. It's not mandatory to use this command, as the request will be automatically finished when WaitFastCGIRequest() is called again, or when the thread ends. entries.d: Initializes FastCGI support. Once called, all the CGI commands switch automatically to FastCGI support. This library support threaded FastCGI processing, when enabling the 'thread-mode' in PureBasic. FastCGI support is only supported through a local socket. InitCGI needs to be called before using this command. Unlike a regular CGI program which is launched at every request, the FastCGI program stays in memory once launched and can handle any number of requests. It can be very useful if the CGI initialization is time consumming (for example connecting a database), so it's only performed once at start.

entries.d: Executes a SQL query on the given database. Only queries which doesn't change the database records are accepted ('SELECT' like queries). To performs database modification, use DatabaseUpdate.

entries.d: Open the specified dialog and display it on the screen. To access the dialog gadgets use DialogGadget. To get the window number of this dialog use DialogWindow. UseDialogScintillaGadget, UseDialogOpenGLGadget, UseDialogWebGadget and UseDialogWebViewGadget can be used to enable support for these gadgets in the dialog lib. They are not enabled by default to reduce the dialog library size footprint.

entries.s: Result = XmlDialogGadget(#Dialog, #XML, Name$ [, x, y [, Width, Height]])
entries.d: Creates the specified dialog as a gadget (a ContainerGadget), instead of opening it as its own window like OpenXMLDialog does. This allows a dialog defined in XML to be embedded inside an existing window, next to other gadgets. It uses exactly the same XML format as OpenXMLDialog (see its documentation for the full XML reference) - the very same XML document can be used with either command: the root <window> element becomes the created ContainerGadget, and any window-only attribute or flag it may still carry (title, screencentered, systemmenu, ...) is simply ignored. The gadget is created inside the currently active window, exactly like ContainerGadget itself, so XmlDialogGadget has to be called after opening (or after selecting, with UseGadgetList) the window that should host it. To access the dialog gadgets, including the root gadget itself, use DialogGadget (give the root <window> element a 'name' attribute in the XML to retrieve it). Unlike a dialog opened with OpenXMLDialog, DialogWindow returns -1 for a dialog created with XmlDialogGadget, as it has no window of its own. UseDialogScintillaGadget, UseDialogOpenGLGadget, UseDialogWebGadget and UseDialogWebViewGadget can be used to enable support for these gadgets in the dialog lib. They are not enabled by default to reduce the dialog library size footprint.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the dialog gadget has been successfully created, returns zero otherwise. To get more information about the error which has occurred, use DialogError.

entries.d: Starts a Drag & Drop operation with a list of filenames.

Note that unlike with the other functions that start Drag & Drop, nothing should be done when #PB_Drag_Move is returned. As the dragged data is only the filename and not the file itself, any action that is taken on the file must be done by the drag target.

entries.d: Starts a Drag & Drop operation with a list of custom data formats. The types of formats available and the way in which they are represented depends on the Operating system. This function offers the possibility to work with formats not natively supported by PureBasic, while still using the simple mechanisms provided by this library to carry out the Drag & Drop operation.
entries.r: Returns one of the above Drag & Drop action values to indicate what action the user took, or #PB_Drag_None if the user aborted the Drag & Drop operation. Note that if #PB_Drag_Move is returned, it is your responsibility to remove the dragged data from your application.

entries.d: Starts a "private" Drag & Drop operation. Unlike the other functions that start Drag & Drop, this data can only be dropped inside the application (Data dragged with functions like DragText or DragImage can be accepted by other applications as well). This function should be used to add Drag & Drop functionality between Gadgets or Windows with data that would not be understood by other applications.
entries.r: Returns one of the above Drag & Drop action values to indicate what action the user took, or #PB_Drag_None if the user aborted the Drag & Drop operation.

entries.d: Enables a window to be a target for Drag & Drop operations of a specific format. Only the area not covered by any gadgets will be the target area. When the user drags data of this format over the window, the cursor will indicate that the data can be dropped there.
entries.r: None

entries.d: After a #PB_Event_GadgetDrop or #PB_Event_WindowDrop is received by WaitWindowEvent or WindowEvent, this function returns the action that should be taken with the data.
entries.r: Returns one of the following values: #PB_Drag_Copy: The data should be copied #PB_Drag_Move: The data should be moved (The drag source is responsible for removing the original data) #PB_Drag_Link: The data should be linked

entries.r: Returns the memory address where the dropped data is located. The EventDropSize command returns the size of this buffer.

entries.r: Returns a list of filenames or directories, all with full path. The individual names are separated by a Chr(10) (linefeed) character.

entries.d: After a #PB_Event_GadgetDrop or #PB_Event_WindowDrop is received by WaitWindowEvent or WindowEvent with a format (can be get with EventDropType) of #PB_Drop_Image, this function can be used to retrieve the dropped image.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the image was successfully created and zero if not. If #PB_Any was used for the #Image parameter then the generated number is returned on success.

entries.d: After a #PB_Event_GadgetDrop or #PB_Event_WindowDrop is received by WaitWindowEvent or WindowEvent with a format (can be get with EventDropType) of #PB_Drop_Private, this function returns the 'PrivateType' that was dropped.

entries.d: Add a new absolute or relative path to the current 3D path list. All the 3D functions which need to load data (e.g. texture, mesh, sky, world) will use this path. It needs to be put after OpenScreen or OpenWindowedScreen. You may wonder why there is a special way to handle the files for 3D functions? Because it makes the data access more flexible and now, you can access the data using the standard filesystem or directly via the archive file like a .zip file. It's a very cool feature because you can pack all your data in one big compressed file, and then access the assets as if these were contained a standard directory.

entries.d: This function loads an entire world. Currently, the Quake3 BSP format is the only one supported but more formats will follow. The Filename$ must be accessible in the 3D path, so the Add3DArchive function should be used before calling this function. A world can be easily created using third party tools like 'Quark'. A world can contain a sky, building, lights and more. Actually, all Quake 3 maps can be loaded out of the box with full detail. If the 'Result' is 0, the world could not be loaded. The BSP format is owned by iD Software and can only be used in freeware programs. Commercial software must acquire a license from iD to use this format. The license scheme is beyond PureBasic and Fantaisie Software can't be responsible for the incorrect use of this function.

The entity pick is based on its bounding box, not on its mesh. To get more information about the picked object position, use PickX, PickY and PickZ.

This function relies on the physic engine, which needs to be activated with EnableWorldPhysics before using this command. Only entities with bodies will react to the ray. entries.r: Returns the read value or zero if there was an error.

entries.d: Read a quad (8 bytes) from a file, starting at the current file position.
entries.r: Returns the read number or zero if there was an error.

entries.d: Read a string from a file until an 'End Of Line' or a 'Null' character is found (Unix, DOS and Macintosh file formats are supported).
entries.r: Returns the read string, or an empty string if the read has failed.

entries.d: Checks if the current file position contains a BOM (Byte Order Mark) and tries to identify the String encoding used in the file.
entries.r: Returns one of the following values: #PB_Ascii : No BOM detected. This usually means a plain text file. #PB_UTF8 : UTF-8 BOM detected. #PB_Unicode: UTF-16 (little endian) BOM detected. #PB_UTF16BE: UTF-16 (big endian) BOM detected. #PB_UTF32 : UTF-32 (little endian) BOM detected. #PB_UTF32BE: UTF-32 (big endian) BOM detected. The #PB_Ascii, #PB_UTF8 and #PB_Unicode results may be used directly in further calls to ReadString to read the file. The other results represent string formats that cannot be directly read with PureBasic string functions. They are included for completeness so that an application can display a proper error-message.

entries.d: Read a unicode character (2 bytes) from a file, starting at the current file position.
entries.r: Returns the read character or zero if there was an error.

entries.d: Read a word (2 bytes) from a file, starting at the current file position.
entries.r: Returns the read number or zero if there was an error.

entries.d: Cuts the file at the current file position and discards all data that follows.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Write an ASCII character (1 byte) to a file.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.

entries.d: Write a byte number (1 byte) to a file.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.

entries.d: Write a character number (1 byte in ASCII, 2 bytes in unicode) to a file.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful or zero if it failed.

entries.d: Write the content of the specified memory buffer to a file.
entries.r: Returns the number of bytes actually written to the file. If there is an error, the return-value is zero.

entries.d: Write a double number (8 bytes) to a file.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.

entries.d: Write a float number (4 bytes) to a file.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.

entries.d: Write an integer number (4 bytes in 32-bit executable, 8 bytes in 64-bit executable) to a file.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.

entries.d: Write a long number (4 bytes) to a file.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.

entries.d: Write a quad number (8 bytes) to a file.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.

entries.d: Write a string to a file.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.

entries.d: Writes a BOM (Byte Order Mark) at the current position in the file.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.

entries.d: Write a string to a file and add an 'end of line' character.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.

entries.d: Write a unicode character (2 bytes) to a file.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.

entries.d: Write a word number (2 bytes) to a file.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.

entries.d: Checks if the specified Filename$ doesn't contain invalid characters for the file-system. For example, on Windows '/' and '\' characters are not allowed in the filename.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the filename does not contain invalid characters and zero if it does.

entries.d: Copy the contents of the source directory to the destination.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.

entries.d: Copy the source file to the destination.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful or zero if it failed.

entries.d: Creates a new directory.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful or zero if it failed.

entries.d: Deletes the specified Directory$ or files in that Directory$ matching the provided pattern.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful or zero if it failed.

entries.d: Deletes the specified file.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful or zero if it failed.

entries.d: Returns the attributes of the current entry in the directory being listed with ExamineDirectory and NextDirectoryEntry functions.
entries.r: Returns the attributes of the current file. On Windows, Attributes is a combination of the following values: #PB_FileSystem_Hidden : File is hidden #PB_FileSystem_Archive : File has been changed and not archived since the last time #PB_FileSystem_Compressed: File is compressed #PB_FileSystem_Normal : Normal attributes #PB_FileSystem_ReadOnly : File is in read-only mode #PB_FileSystem_System : File is a system file On Linux or MacOSX, Attributes is a combination of these values: #PB_FileSystem_Link : The file is a symbolic link #PB_FileSystem_ReadUser : Access flags for the owning user #PB_FileSystem_WriteUser #PB_FileSystem_ExecUser #PB_FileSystem_ReadGroup : Access flags for the owning user's group #PB_FileSystem_WriteGroup #PB_FileSystem_ExecGroup #PB_FileSystem_ReadAll : Access flags for all other users #PB_FileSystem_WriteAll #PB_FileSystem_ExecAll

entries.d: Returns the date of the current entry in the directory being listed with ExamineDirectory and NextDirectoryEntry functions.
entries.r: Returns the specified date of the current directory entry in the format of the PureBasic Date library.

entries.d: Returns the name of the current entry in the directory being listed with ExamineDirectory and NextDirectoryEntry functions.
entries.r: Returns the name of the current directory entry.

entries.d: Returns the size of the current entry in the directory being listed with ExamineDirectory and NextDirectoryEntry functions.
entries.r: Returns the size of the current directory entry in bytes.

entries.d: Returns the type of the current entry in the directory being listed with ExamineDirectory and NextDirectoryEntry functions.
entries.r: Returns one of the following values: #PB_DirectoryEntry_File : This entry is a file. #PB_DirectoryEntry_Directory: This entry is a directory.

entries.d: Start to examine a directory for listing with the functions NextDirectoryEntry, DirectoryEntryName and DirectoryEntryType.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the directory can be enumerated or zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any was used as the #Directory parameter then the generated directory number is returned.

entries.d: Returns the size of the specified file. This function can also be used to check if a file or directory exists or not.
entries.r: Returns the size of the file in bytes, or one of the following values: -1: File not found. -2: File is a directory.

entries.d: Finish the enumeration started with ExamineDirectory. This frees the resources associated with the #Directory listing.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Returns the current directory for the program.
entries.r: Returns the full path of the current directory. It will end with a path separator #PS, #PS$ ('\' for Windows or '/' otherwise). It's very unlikely, but if this function fails, it will return an empty string.

entries.d: Retrieves the file extension part of a full path.
entries.r: Returns the file extension. For example, if the full path is "C:\PureBasic\PB.exe", the result will be "exe".

entries.d: Returns the attributes of the given file.
entries.r: Returns the attributes of the file. If the file does not exist or the attributes cannot be read, the result is the value -1. On Windows, Attributes is a combination of the following values: #PB_FileSystem_Hidden : File is hidden #PB_FileSystem_Archive : File has been changed and not archived since the last time #PB_FileSystem_Compressed: File is compressed #PB_FileSystem_Normal : Normal attributes #PB_FileSystem_ReadOnly : File is in read-only mode #PB_FileSystem_System : File is a system file On Linux or MacOSX, Attributes is a combination of these values: #PB_FileSystem_Link : The file is a symbolic link #PB_FileSystem_ReadUser : Access flags for the owning user #PB_FileSystem_WriteUser #PB_FileSystem_ExecUser #PB_FileSystem_ReadGroup : Access flags for the owning user's group #PB_FileSystem_WriteGroup #PB_FileSystem_ExecGroup #PB_FileSystem_ReadAll : Access flags for all other users #PB_FileSystem_WriteAll #PB_FileSystem_ExecAll

entries.d: Returns the date of the specified file.
entries.r: Returns the requested date in the format of the PureBasic Date library.

entries.d: Retrieves the file part of a full path.
entries.r: Returns the file name. For example, if the full path is "C:\PureBasic\PB.exe", the result will be "PB.exe".

entries.d: Returns the home directory path of the currently logged user.
entries.r: Returns the full path of the home directory. It will end with a path separator #PS, #PS$ ('\' for Windows or '/' otherwise). It's very unlikely, but if this function fails, it will return an empty string.

entries.d: Retrieves the path part of a full path.
entries.r: Returns the path part. For example, if the full path is "C:\PureBasic\PB.exe", the result will be "C:\PureBasic\".

entries.d: Returns the temporary directory name.
entries.r: Returns the full path to the temporary directory. It will end with a path separator #PS, #PS$ ('\' for Windows or '/' otherwise). It's very unlikely, but if this function fails, it will return an empty string.

entries.d: Returns the directory path of the specified directory type.
entries.r: Returns the full path of the specified directory. It will end with a path separator #PS, #PS$ ('\' for Windows or '/' otherwise). If the type is not found it will return an empty string.

entries.d: Tests if the given directory number is a valid and correctly initialized directory enumeration.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the given input is a valid enumeration and zero otherwise.

entries.d: This function must be called after an ExamineDirectory. It will go step-by-step into the directory and list its contents.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if a new entry was read from the directory and zero if there are no more entries.

entries.d: Rename the old file to the new file.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the operation succeeded and zero if it failed.

entries.d: Changes the current directory for the program.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the current directory has been successfully changed, return zero otherwise.

entries.d: Set the attributes of the given Filename$.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero otherwise.

entries.d: Changes the date of the specified file.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero otherwise.

entries.d: Returns the unique system identifier of the #Font.
entries.r: Returns the unique system ID of the font. This result is sometimes also referred to as a 'Handle'. Take a look at the extra chapter Handles and Numbers for more information.

entries.d: Free the given Font, previously loaded with LoadFont.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Tests if the given #Font is a valid and correctly initialized font.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if #Font is a valid font and zero otherwise.

entries.d: Tries to open the specified font.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the font was loaded successfully and zero if not. If #PB_Any was used for the #Font parameter then the generated number is returned on success.

entries.d: Register a font file for use with the LoadFont command. All fonts contained in the file are then available.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the file was successfully registered, zero otherwise.

entries.d: Aborts the current background file transfer previously started with SendFTPFile or ReceiveFTPFile. If no file transfer is in progress, this function has no effect.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Checks if the specified #Ftp connection is still connected to the server.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the connection is still open and zero if the server closed the connection.

entries.d: Closes the specified #Ftp client connection previously opened with OpenFTP and free any associated resources.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Creates a new directory on the FTP server.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.

entries.d: Deletes a directory on the FTP server.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the directory was deleted or zero if the operation failed.

entries.d: Deletes a file on the FTP server.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the file was deleted or zero if the operation failed.

entries.d: Starts to examine the content of the current FTP directory.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the operation succeeded or zero if it failed.

entries.d: Finishes the enumeration started with ExamineFTPDirectory. This allows to free the resources associated with the FTP listing.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Returns the attributes of the current entry in the FTP enumeration being listed with the ExamineFTPDirectory and NextFTPDirectoryEntry functions.
entries.r: Returns a combination of the following values: #PB_FTP_ReadUser : Access flags for the owning user #PB_FTP_WriteUser #PB_FTP_ExecuteUser #PB_FTP_ReadGroup : Access flags for the owning user's group #PB_FTP_WriteGroup #PB_FTP_ExecuteGroup #PB_FTP_ReadAll : Access flags for all other users #PB_FTP_WriteAll #PB_FTP_ExecuteAll

entries.d: Returns the date of the current entry in the FTP enumeration being listed with ExamineFTPDirectory and NextFTPDirectoryEntry functions.
entries.r: Returns the date of the entry in the format of the Date library.

entries.d: Returns the name of the current entry in the FTP enumeration being listed with ExamineFTPDirectory and NextFTPDirectoryEntry functions.
entries.r: Returns the entry name.

entries.d: Returns the raw line of the current entry in the FTP enumeration being listed with ExamineFTPDirectory and NextFTPDirectoryEntry functions, as it has been sent by the FTP server. It can be useful when the server isn't supported by ExamineFTPDirectory, so the information about the directory listing can still be retrieved and parsed accordingly.
entries.r: Returns the entry line as sent by the FTP server.

entries.d: Returns the size of the current entry in the FTP enumeration being listed with ExamineFTPDirectory and NextFTPDirectoryEntry functions.
entries.r: Returns the size in bytes.

entries.d: Returns the type of the current entry in the FTP enumeration being listed with ExamineFTPDirectory and NextFTPDirectoryEntry functions.
entries.r: Returns one of the following constants: #PB_FTP_File : This entry is a file. #PB_FTP_Directory: This entry is a directory.

entries.d: Returns the progress of the current file transfer, started either with ReceiveFTPFile or SendFTPFile.
entries.r: Returns the actual number of bytes which has been received/sent or one of the following values: #PB_FTP_Started : The file transfer is in the initialization phase. #PB_FTP_Finished: The file transfer is finished correctly. #PB_FTP_Error : The file transfer is finished but an error occurred.

entries.d: Returns the current FTP directory.
entries.r: Return the current FTP directory, relative to the FTP root.

entries.d: Tests if the given #Ftp number is a valid and correctly initialized ftp client.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the given number is a valid and correctly initialized client connection.

entries.d: Moves to the next entry in an enumeration started with ExamineFTPDirectory.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the next entry is available or zero if there are no more entries to examine.

entries.s: Result = OpenFTP(#Ftp, ServerName$, User$, Password$ [, Flags [, Port]])
entries.d: Tries to open a connection on the specified FTP or SFTP server.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the connection was established correctly and zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any is used as the #Ftp parameter then the generated number for the connection is returned on success.

entries.d: Receives a file from a FTP server.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the file was downloaded correctly, or the asynchronous transfer was initialized correctly. On failure, the return-value is zero.

entries.d: Renames a file on the FTP server.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the file was renamed successfully and zero otherwise.

entries.d: Sends a file to a FTP server.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the file was uploaded correctly, or the asynchronous transfer was initialized correctly. On failure, the return-value is zero.

entries.d: Changes the current #Ftp directory, relative to the current directory.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.

entries.d: Adds a new column to the specified gadget.
entries.r: None

entries.s: Result = AddGadgetItem(#Gadget, Position, Text$ [, ImageID [, Flags]])
entries.d: Add a new item to the specified gadget.
entries.r: The return-value is only valid with the MDIGadget. If #PB_Any was used as the 'Position' parameter when adding an item to the MDIGadget, the return-value is the number that identifies the new MDI window.

entries.d: Bind a gadget event to a callback. It's an additional way to handle events in PureBasic, which works without problem with the regulars WindowEvent / WaitWindowEvent commands. It also allows to have real-time event notifications as the callback can be invoked as soon as the event occurs (useful for ScrollBarGadget, ScrollAreaGadget etc.). A gadget event can be unbound with UnbindGadgetEvent.
entries.r: None

entries.s: Result = ButtonGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height, Text$ [, Flags])
entries.d: Create a button gadget in the current GadgetList.
entries.r: Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.

entries.s: Result = ButtonImageGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height, ImageID [, Flags])
entries.d: Create a button gadget with an image in the current GadgetList.
entries.r: Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.

entries.s: Result = CalendarGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height [, Date [, Flags]])
entries.d: Create a calendar gadget in the current GadgetList. This gadget displays a month calendar and lets the user select a date.
entries.r: Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.

entries.s: Result = CanvasGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height [, Flags])
entries.d: Create a canvas gadget in the current GadgetList. This gadget provides a drawing surface without alpha channel and events for mouse and keyboard interaction to easily create custom views.
entries.r: Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.

entries.d: Returns the OutputID of a CanvasGadget to perform 2D rendering operation on it.
entries.r: Returns the output ID or zero if drawing is not possible. This value should be passed directly to the StartDrawing function to start the drawing operation. The return-value is valid only for one drawing operation and cannot be reused.

entries.d: Returns the OutputID of a CanvasGadget to perform vector drawing operations on it.
entries.r: Returns the output ID or zero if drawing is not possible. This value should be passed directly to the StartVectorDrawing function to start the drawing operation. The return-value is valid only for one drawing operation and cannot be reused.

entries.s: Result = CheckBoxGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height, Text$ [, Flags])
entries.d: Create a checkbox gadget in the current GadgetList.
entries.r: Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.

entries.d: Clears all the items from the specified gadget.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Terminate the current gadget list creation and go back to the previous GadgetList.
entries.r: None

entries.s: Result = ComboBoxGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height [, Flags])
entries.d: Create a ComboBox gadget in the current GadgetList.
entries.r: Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.

entries.s: Result = ContainerGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height [, Flags])
entries.d: Creates a container gadget in the current GadgetList. It's a simple panel gadget which can contain other gadgets.
entries.r: Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.

entries.d: Returns the number of items in the specified gadget.
entries.r: Returns the number of items in the gadget.

entries.s: Result = DateGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height [, Mask$ [, Date [, Flags]]])
entries.d: Creates a String gadget in the current GadgetList, in which a date and/or time can be entered.
entries.r: Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.

entries.d: Disable or enable the gadget.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Disables or enables the redrawing of a gadget. When a large number of items is added to a gadget such as ListIconGadget, TreeGadget or ListViewGadget, each insertion normally triggers a repaint which can make the update slow and flickering. Disabling the redraw before the mass update and enabling it again afterwards performs a single repaint once all the items are in place. Every call which disables the redraw must be paired with a call which enables it again. Enabling the redraw automatically refreshes the gadget content. The current selection and scroll position are kept across the operation.
entries.r: None

entries.s: Result = EditorGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height [, Flags])
entries.d: Creates an Editor gadget in the current GadgetList.
entries.r: Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.

entries.s: Result = ExplorerComboGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height, Directory$, [, Flags])
entries.d: Creates a ComboBox that lets you display a path and all its parent folders, so the user can choose one of them. You can find such a ComboBox, for example, in the OpenFileRequester.
entries.r: Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.

entries.s: Result = ExplorerListGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height, Directory$, [, Flags])
entries.d: Creates a listing of a directory just as Explorer does. It lets the user choose a file or a folder and (if you do not prevent it by a flag) navigate through the whole directory tree.
entries.r: Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.

entries.s: Result = ExplorerTreeGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height, Directory$, [, Flags])
entries.d: Creates a tree listing of the directory tree just as Explorer does. It lets the user navigate through his file-system, and choose a file or folder.
entries.r: Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.

entries.s: Result = FrameGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height, Text$ [, Flags])
entries.d: Creates a Frame gadget in the current GadgetList. This kind of gadget is decorative only.
entries.r: Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.

entries.d: Free and remove the gadget from the display (and free its gadgetlist if the gadget was a container).
entries.r: None

entries.r: Returns the height of the gadget in pixels.

entries.d: Returns the unique system identifier of the #Gadget.
entries.r: Returns the system identifier. This result is sometimes also known as 'Handle'. Look at the extra chapter Handles and Numbers for more information.

entries.d: Returns the OS handle for the given item in a gadget. This is especially useful for use with the OS API.
entries.r: Returns the OS handle for the item or zero on failure.

entries.d: Associate the specified Text$ with the #Gadget. A tooltip text is text which is displayed when the mouse cursor is over the gadget for a small amount of time (typically a yellow floating box).
entries.r: None

entries.d: Returns the width of the specified gadget.
entries.r: Returns the width of the gadget in pixels.

entries.d: Returns the X position of the specified gadget.
entries.r: Returns the X position relative to the gadgets parent or window (in pixels).

entries.d: Returns the Y position of the specified gadget.
entries.r: Returns the Y position relative to the gadgets parent or window in pixels.

entries.d: Returns the gadget number of the Gadget that currently has the keyboard focus.
entries.r: Returns the #Gadget number of the Gadget with the focus. If no Gadget has the focus, -1 is returned.

entries.d: Gets an attribute value of the specified gadget.
entries.r: Returns the value of the specified gadget attribute or 0 if the gadget does not support the attribute.

entries.r: Returns the attribute value or zero if the item or attribute does not exist.

entries.d: Returns a color setting from the specified gadget item.
entries.r: Returns the current color setting. This function returns the color that was previously set by SetGadgetItemColor. If no custom color is set for the #Gadget and ColorType, the function returns #PB_Default.

entries.d: Returns the value that was previously stored with this gadget item with the SetGadgetItemData function. This allows to associate a custom value with the items of a gadget.

entries.d: Returns the item state of the specified gadget.
entries.r: Returns the state of the gadget item or 0 if there is an error. See below for the meaning of this value depending on the gadget type.

entries.d: Returns the item text of the specified gadget.

entries.d: Returns the current state of the gadget.

entries.d: Returns the gadget text content of the specified gadget.
entries.r: Returns the gadget text, or an empty string if the gadget does not support text content.

entries.d: Hide or show a gadget.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Aborts the progress of the specified asynchronous download, started either with ReceiveHTTPFile or ReceiveHTTPMemory. It's also usable for HTTPRequest and HTTPRequestMemory (if #PB_HTTP_Asynchronous was used).

entries.d: Free the resources associated to the specified asynchronous download, started either with ReceiveHTTPFile or ReceiveHTTPMemory. It must be always called after a successful call of ReceiveHTTPFile or ReceiveHTTPMemory.
entries.r: Depending on which Receive command was used to start the download, FinishHTTP() returns one of the following results: ReceiveHTTPFile: Amount of received bytes (size of the stored file). ReceiveHTTPMemory with the #PB_HTTP_Asynchronous flag set: Address of the memory area where the received data was stored. With MemorySize the amount of received data can be determined then.

entries.d: Get a specific part of the given URL$. This can be a named parameter in the URL string or another part of the URL.

entries.d: Returns a memory buffer containing the whole response of an HTTP request created with HTTPRequest or HTTPRequestMemory. Once done with it, the buffer needs to be freed with FreeMemory. If the flag #PB_HTTP_Asynchronous was used when calling HTTPRequest or HTTPRequestMemory, this command is only valid if the request has been successful.
entries.r: A memory buffer containing the whole response of an HTTP request. Once done with it, the buffer needs to be freed with FreeMemory.

entries.d: Returns the progress of the specified asynchronous download, started either with ReceiveHTTPFile or ReceiveHTTPMemory.
entries.r: The status of the download. It can be the current number of received bytes or one of the following values: #PB_HTTP_Success : the download has been successfully finished. #PB_HTTP_Failed : the download has failed. #PB_HTTP_Aborted : the download has been aborted with AbortHTTP.

entries.d: Specify a proxy to use for the following HTTP commands: ReceiveHTTPFile, ReceiveHTTPMemory, HTTPRequest and HTTPRequestMemory.
entries.r: None

entries.s: Result = HTTPRequest(Type, URL$ [, Data$ [, Flags [, Headers()]]])
entries.d: Send an HTTP request with optional text data. If binary data needs to be sent, HTTPRequestMemory can be used. This command is designed to handle REST like web APIs easily. FinishHTTP needs to be always called once the request has been executed.
entries.r: Returns the HTTP request identifier if the call has been successfully initialized, zero otherwise. HTTPInfo can be used to get some info about the request. If #PB_HTTP_Asynchronous was specified, HTTPProgress can be used and AbortHTTP must be used. HTTPMemory can be used to get the result as a raw buffer (the raw buffer must be freed with FreeMemory). FinishHTTP has to be always called to finish a successfully initialized HTTP request, even if the call was synchronous.

entries.s: Result = HTTPRequestMemory(Type, URL$ [, *Data, DataSize [, Flags [, Headers()]]])
entries.d: Send an HTTP request with optional binary data. If text only data needs to be sent HTTPRequest can be used. This command is designed to handle REST like web API easily. FinishHTTP needs to be always called once the request has been executed.
entries.r: Returns the HTTP request identifier if the call has been successfully initialized, zero otherwise. HTTPInfo can be used to get some info about the request. If #PB_HTTP_Asynchronous was specified, HTTPProgress and AbortHTTP can be used. HTTPMemory can be used to get the result as a raw buffer (the raw buffer must be freed with FreeMemory). FinishHTTP has to be always called to finish a successfully initialized HTTP request, even if the call was synchronous.

entries.d: Specify timeout to use for the following HTTP commands: ReceiveHTTPFile, ReceiveHTTPMemory, HTTPRequest and HTTPRequestMemory.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Download a file to disk from the given URL$.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the download was successful, zero otherwise. If #PB_HTTP_Asynchronous was specified, it returns the 'HttpConnection' value needed for HTTPProgress, AbortHTTP and FinishHTTP. When using #PB_HTTP_Asynchronous, FinishHTTP needs to be called when the download is finished (successfully or not).

entries.d: Download a file to a new memory buffer from the given URL$.
entries.r: Returns the new memory buffer address if the download was successful, zero otherwise. MemorySize can be used to get the size of the downloaded item. The memory buffer needs to be freed with FreeMemory once finished using it. If #PB_HTTP_Asynchronous was specified, it returns the 'HttpConnection' value needed for HTTPProgress, AbortHTTP and FinishHTTP. When using #PB_HTTP_Asynchronous, FinishHTTP needs to be called when the download is finished (successfully or not).

entries.d: Set a specific part of the given URL$.
entries.r: Returns the modified URL.

entries.d: Returns a decoded URL$ which has been encoded with the HTTP format.
entries.r: Returns the decoded URL.

entries.d: Returns the URL$ encoded to the HTTP format.
entries.r: Returns the encoded URL. To convert an encoded URL back to a unencoded format, use URLDecoder

entries.d: Adds a new frame to the specified image. The new frame will have the same dimension and depth like the image.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the new frame has been successfully created, zero otherwise.

entries.d: Load the specified image from the given memory area.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the image was loaded successfully and zero if the image could not be loaded. If #PB_Any was specified as the #Image parameter then the auto-generated number is returned on success.

entries.d: Creates an identical copy of an image. If the image is multi-frame, the current frame will be used for the copy.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the image was copied successfully and zero if the copy could not be created. If #PB_Any was specified as the #Image2 parameter then the auto-generated number is returned on success.

entries.s: Result = CreateImage(#Image, Width, Height [, Depth [, BackColor]])
entries.d: Create an empty image (with black background) which can be used to do rendering on it.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the image was created successfully and zero if the image could not be created. If #PB_Any was specified as the #Image parameter then the auto-generated number is returned on success.

entries.d: Encode the specified image into a memory buffer.
entries.r: Returns a pointer to a newly allocated memory buffer containing the encoded image, or zero if the encoding has failed. MemorySize can be used to get the size of the encoded image. FreeMemory has to be used to free the buffer after use.

entries.d: Free the specified image and release its associated memory.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Gets the current frame index of the image.
entries.r: The current frame index (starting from 0). If the image is not multi-frame, it will always return 0.

entries.d: Returns the display delay (in milliseconds) for the current image frame. Each frame can have its own delay.
entries.r: Returns the display delay (in milliseconds) for the current image frame.

entries.s: Result = GrabImage(#Image1, #Image2, x, y, Width, Height)
entries.d: Create a new image with the selected area on the source image. If the image is multi-frame, the current frame will be used for the grab.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the image was created successfully and zero if the image could not be created. If #PB_Any was specified as the #Image2 parameter then the auto-generated number is returned on success.

entries.d: Returns the depth of the #Image, as it is stored internally by PureBasic.
entries.r: Returns one of the possible depth values described above.

entries.d: Return the original image format.
entries.r: Returns the image original format. It can be one of the following value: #PB_ImagePlugin_JPEG #PB_ImagePlugin_JPEG2000 #PB_ImagePlugin_PNG #PB_ImagePlugin_TGA #PB_ImagePlugin_TIFF #PB_ImagePlugin_BMP #PB_ImagePlugin_ICON #PB_ImagePlugin_GIF #PB_ImagePlugin_WEBP If the image was not loaded from one of these formats, it will return zero. This is the case for images created with CreateImage or GrabImage.

entries.d: Returns the number of frames of the image.
entries.r: Returns the frame count of the image. If the image is not multi-frame, it will always return 1.

entries.d: Returns the height of the given image.
entries.r: Returns the height of the image in pixels.

entries.d: Returns the ImageID of the image.
entries.r: Returns the operating system handle of the image.

entries.d: Returns the OutputID of the image to perform 2D rendering operation on it. Alternatively, the ImageVectorOutput command can be used to perform vector drawing on the image. If the image is multi-frame, the current frame will be used.
entries.r: Returns the output ID or zero if drawing is not possible. This value should be passed directly to the StartDrawing function to start the drawing operation. The return-value is valid only for one drawing operation and cannot be reused.

entries.d: Returns the OutputID of the image to perform 2D vector drawing operations on it. If the image is multi-frame, the current frame will be used.
entries.r: Returns the output ID or zero if drawing is not possible. This value should be passed directly to the StartVectorDrawing function to start the drawing operation. The return-value is valid only for one drawing operation and cannot be reused.

entries.d: Returns the width of the given image.
entries.r: Returns the width of the image in pixels.

entries.d: Tests if the given image number is a valid and correctly initialized image.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if #Image is a valid image and zero if not.

entries.d: Load the specified image from a file.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the image was loaded successfully and zero if the image could not be loaded. If #PB_Any was specified as the #Image parameter then the auto-generated number is returned on success.

entries.d: Removes the specified frame from the image.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the frame has been successfully removed, zero otherwise.

entries.d: Resize the #Image to the given dimension.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the operation succeeded and zero if it failed.

entries.r: None

entries.d: Sets the display delay (in milliseconds) for the current image frame. Each frame can have its own delay.
entries.r: Sets the display delay (in milliseconds) for the current image frame.

entries.d: Enables the GIF image support for the CatchImage, LoadImage, CatchSprite and LoadSprite functions. Only LoadImage and CatchImage support multi-frame GIF (it will result in a multi-frame image).

entries.d: Enables the JPEG 2000 image support for the CatchImage, LoadImage, CatchSprite and LoadSprite functions.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Enables the JPEG 2000 image support for the SaveImage and SaveSprite functions.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Enables the JPEG (Joint Picture Expert Group) image support for the CatchImage, LoadImage, CatchSprite and LoadSprite functions.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Enables the JPEG (Joint Picture Expert Group) image support for the SaveImage and SaveSprite functions.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Enables image loading through the imaging library provided by the operating system for the CatchImage, LoadImage, CatchSprite and LoadSprite functions. The following system libraries are used: GDI+ on Windows, ImageIO on macOS and GdkPixbuf (or Qt) on Linux. As no decoder is embedded in the executable, this plugin adds almost no code to the final program, and the list of supported formats as well as their security fixes automatically follow the operating system updates. A single call to this function replaces UseJPEGImageDecoder, UsePNGImageDecoder, UseGIFImageDecoder and the other individual decoders. It can still be combined with them: the automatic image format detection will pick the right decoder for each file.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Enables image saving through the imaging library provided by the operating system for the SaveImage and SaveSprite functions. The following system libraries are used: GDI+ on Windows, ImageIO on macOS and GdkPixbuf (or Qt) on Linux. As no encoder is embedded in the executable, this plugin adds almost no code to the final program. This single call provides the encoders for the #PB_ImagePlugin_JPEG, #PB_ImagePlugin_PNG, #PB_ImagePlugin_BMP, #PB_ImagePlugin_TIFF and #PB_ImagePlugin_GIF constants of SaveImage, so for example SaveImage with #PB_ImagePlugin_JPEG works without UseJPEGImageEncoder. If a dedicated encoder (such as UseJPEGImageEncoder) is also used, that one takes precedence.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Enables the PNG (Portable Network Graphic) image support for SaveImage and SaveSprite.

entries.d: Enables the TGA (Targa) image support for the CatchImage, LoadImage, CatchSprite and LoadSprite functions.

entries.d: Enables the TIFF image support for the CatchImage, LoadImage, CatchSprite and LoadSprite functions.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Enables the WebP image support for the CatchImage, LoadImage, CatchSprite and LoadSprite functions.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Enables the WebP image support for the SaveImage and SaveSprite functions.
entries.r: None

entries.s: Result = ConeTwistJoint(#Joint, EntityID, TransformX, TransformY, TransformZ, EntityID2, TransformX2, TransformY2, TransformZ2)

entries.d: Get the specified attribute value of the given joint and its associated entities.
entries.r: Returns the value of the specified attribute or 0 if the joint does not support the attribute.

entries.d: Creates a new hinge joint between the two given entities. Hinge can be used to simulate door, moving bridge etc.

entries.d: Updates the current joystick state. It needs to be called before using the following functions: JoystickButton, JoystickAxisX, JoystickAxisY and JoystickAxisZ.

entries.d: Add a new array element to a JSON value of type #PB_JSON_Array.
entries.r: Returns the address of the added JSON value. The newly added value initially has type #PB_JSON_Null.

entries.d: Parse JSON data from a memory buffer. The contents of the memory buffer are expected to be encoded in UTF-8 format. The JSONValue function can be used to access the contained JSON value(s) after parsing.
entries.r: Nonzero if the JSON data was parsed correctly, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #JSON parameter then the generated number is returned on success.

entries.d: After a call to NextJSONMember, returns the address of the currently examined JSON object member of the specified JSON value of type #PB_JSON_Object.

entries.d: Returns the number of members in a JSON value of type #PB_JSON_Object.

entries.d: Returns the type of the given JSON value.
entries.r: It can be one of the following: #PB_JSON_Null The value represents the JSON literal null. #PB_JSON_String The value contains a string. GetJSONString can be used to read the string. #PB_JSON_Number The value contains a number. GetJSONDouble, GetJSONFloat, GetJSONInteger or GetJSONQuad can be used to read the number. #PB_JSON_Boolean The value contains a boolean. GetJSONBoolean can be used to read the value. #PB_JSON_Array The value contains an array of JSON elements. JSONArraySize returns the size of the array. GetJSONElement can be used to get a specific array element. AddJSONElement, RemoveJSONElement, ResizeJSONElements or ClearJSONElements can be used to modify the array. #PB_JSON_Object The value contains an object (a set of key/value pairs). JSONObjectSize returns the number of members in the object. GetJSONMember returns a specific member value. ExamineJSONMembers can be used to examine the member values. AddJSONMember, RemoveJSONMember or ClearJSONMembers can be used to modify the object.

entries.d: Parse JSON data from a string. The JSONValue function can be used to access the contained JSON value(s) after parsing.
entries.r: Nonzero if the JSON data was parsed correctly, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #JSON parameter then the generated number is returned on success.

entries.d: Updates the keyboard state. This function has to be called before using KeyboardInkey, KeyboardPushed or KeyboardReleased.

entries.d: Initializes the keyboard environment for later use. This function has to be called before any other function in this library.
entries.r: Nonzero if the keyboard access can be initialized, zero otherwise.

entries.d: Returns the last typed character, very useful when keyboard input is required within a gaming application, such as the name in highscore, in game console, etc.).

entries.d: Changes the current behavior of the keyboard. This function affects KeyboardPushed and KeyboardReleased.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Checks if the specified key is pressed. Any number of keys may be pressed at the same time. The function ExamineKeyboard must be called before this function in order to update the keyboard state. The keyboard behavior can be changed with KeyboardMode. To check if a specified key has been pushed and released, see KeyboardReleased.

entries.d: Checks if the specified key has been pushed and released. This function is useful for switch key checks, like a 'Pause' key in a game (one time the game is paused, next time it will continue). The function ExamineKeyboard must be called before this function to update the keyboard state. The keyboard behavior can be changed with KeyboardMode.
entries.r: Nonzero if the specified key has been pushed and released, zero otherwise.

entries.d: Calls a function, in the specified library, in such a manner that the parameters are handled in the same fashion as a normal 'C' language function.
entries.r: Returns the return-value of the called function or zero if the library does not contain a function with the given name.

entries.d: Calls a function directly, using its address. The function is expected to use the stdcall calling convention (the standard in most DLLs on Windows).

entries.d: Joins all the elements of 'List()' into a single string, using 'Separator$' between each element.
entries.r: Returns the resulting string.

entries.r: Returns the address of the data in the last list element if successful and zero if there if there are no elements in the list.

entries.d: Find out the position of the current element in the list, considering that the first element is at the position 0. This function is very fast, and can be used a lot without performance issue (it doesn't iterate the list but uses a cached value).
entries.r: A number containing the position of the current element within the list. The first element is at position 0, the next at 1 and so on. A value of -1 means there is no current element (either the list is empty or ResetList has been used).

entries.d: Returns the number of elements in the list. It does not change the current element. This function is very fast (it doesn't iterates all the list but uses a cached result) and can be safely used to determine if a list is empty or not.

entries.r: None

entries.r: None
