entries.d: Creates an empty submenu in the current menu.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Changes the specified MenuItem state. This functions allows you to display a 'check mark' next to the menu item text.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Changes the text of the specified menu item.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Changes the specified menu title item text.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Unbind a menu event from a callback. If no matching event callback is found, this command has no effect.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Add a new level of detail (LOD) to the mesh. The #Mesh will be replaced automatically with #MeshLOD (which is often a simplified version of #Mesh, with less details) when displayed above the specified distance from the camera. Several LOD mesh can be used for the same #Mesh depending of the distance.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Add a new submesh to the current mesh previously created with CreateMesh. A mesh can have any number of submeshes. A submesh position is relative to the mesh position. Once a submesh is created, use the following commands to build it: MeshVertexPosition, MeshFace and MeshIndex.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Build automatically one or several level of detail (LOD) for the mesh. The #Mesh will be replaced automatically with less complex mesh when displayed above the specified distance from the camera. If more precise LOD meshes are required, AddMeshManualLOD can be used.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Create the shadow volume for the specified #Mesh. It is required if the mesh needs to cast a shadow. It should be done once the mesh creation is completely done, or the shadow will not match the mesh.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Automatically computes the tangent vectors for all vertices of the specified mesh. Dynamic meshes are not supported (meshes created with the #PB_Mesh_Dynamic flag).
entries.r: None

entries.d: Creates a #NewMesh which is the exact copy of the specified #Mesh. If #PB_Any is used as the '#NewMesh' parameter, then the new mesh number will be returned as 'Result'. Dynamic meshes are not supported for copy (meshes created with the #PB_Mesh_Dynamic flag). If the Result equals 0, then the mesh copy has failed. If #NewMesh already exists, then it is freed and replaced by a new one.

entries.s: Result = CreateCapsule(#Mesh, Radius.f, Height.f [, NbRings, NbSegments, NbHeightSegments)
entries.d: Create a new capsule mesh.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the mesh was created successfully and zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any was used as the #Mesh parameter, then the new generated number is returned on success.

entries.s: Result = CreateCone(#Mesh, Radius.f, Height.f [, NbBaseSegments, NbHeightSegments])
entries.d: Create a new cone.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the mesh was created successfully and zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any was used as the #Mesh parameter, then the new generated number is returned on success.

entries.d: Create a new cube mesh.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the mesh was created successfully and zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any was used as the #Mesh parameter, then the new generated number is returned on success.

entries.s: Result = CreateCylinder(#Mesh, Radius.f, Height.f [, NbBaseSegments, NbHeightSegments, CloseTop])
entries.d: Create a new cylinder mesh.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the mesh was created successfully and zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any was used as the #Mesh parameter then the new generated number is returned on success.

entries.d: Creates a new #Mesh from the specified 2 dimensional array of MeshVertex type. This command allows faster mesh creation than using CreateMesh by preparing an array and submitting in one batch to the command.
Create a new ico-sphere mesh.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the mesh was created successfully and zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any was used as the #Mesh parameter, then the new generated number is returned on success.

entries.s: Result = CreateLine3D(#Mesh, x, y, z, Color, x2, y2, z2, Color2)
entries.d: Create a new 3D line mesh. The line is a wireframe object which can be used to ease debugging. To change the line position, just create it again.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the mesh was created successfully and zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any was used as the #Mesh parameter then the new generated number is returned on success.

entries.d: Creates a new empty #Mesh. After creation, the further commands of this library like MeshVertexPosition or MeshFace can be used to build it.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the mesh was created successfully and zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any was used as the #Mesh parameter, then the new generated number is returned on success.

entries.s: Result = CreatePlane(#Mesh, TileSizeX, TileSizeZ, TileCountX, TileCountZ, TextureRepeatCountX, TextureRepeatCountZ)
entries.d: Create a new plane mesh.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the mesh was created successfully and zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any was used as the #Mesh parameter then the new generated number is returned on success.

entries.d: Create a new sphere mesh.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the mesh was created successfully and zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any was used as the #Mesh parameter then the new generated number is returned on success.

entries.s: Result = CreateTorus(#Mesh, Radius.f, SectionRadius.f, Height.f [, NbSectionSegments, NbCircleSegments)
entries.d: Create a new torus mesh.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the mesh was created successfully and zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any was used as the #Mesh parameter then the new generated number is returned on success.

entries.s: Result = CreateTube(#Mesh, OuterRadius.f, InnerRadius.f, Height.f [, NbBaseSegments, NbHeightSegments)
entries.d: Create a new tube mesh.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the mesh was created successfully and zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any was used as the #Mesh parameter then the new generated number is returned on success.

entries.d: Finish the creation of the current mesh started with CreateMesh.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Free the specified #Mesh. All its associated memory is released and the object may not be used anymore.
entries.r: None

entries.s: Result = GetMeshData(#Mesh, SubMesh, DataArray(), Flags, FirstIndex, LastIndex)
entries.d: Get internal mesh data, like vertices, face etc. Dynamic meshes are not supported (meshes created with the #PB_Mesh_Dynamic flag).
entries.r: Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If success, DataArray() has been resized and contains the mesh information.

entries.d: Tests if the given #Mesh is valid and the mesh has been correctly initialized. This function is bulletproof and may be used with any value. If Result equals zero then the given mesh has not been properly created or initialized. This is the correct way to ensure a mesh is ready to use.
Loads a new mesh. Before loading a mesh, an archive must be specified with Add3DArchive.
entries.r: Nonzero if the mesh was successfully loaded, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #Mesh parameter then the generated number is returned on success.

entries.d: Add a new submesh to the specified #Mesh. A mesh can have any number of submeshes. A submesh position is relative to the mesh position.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Add or update a face to the current mesh previously created with CreateMesh. The specified vertices must exist. The first vertex index starts from 0. The created face is a triangle or a quad. MeshIndex can be used if the number of vertices is more than four.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Returns the unique MeshID of the #Mesh. The use of this function is required especially by the CreateEntity function.

Add or update a single vertex in the mesh being created with CreateMesh or updated with UpdateMesh. It behaves like the command MeshFace, but with an arbitrary number of vertices. When using the mode #PB_Mesh_LineList or #PB_Mesh_LineStrip, there are only two vertices per line, so MeshIndex needs to be used in this case.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Return the number of indexes in the mesh.
entries.r: Returns the number of indexes in the mesh, or zero if the mesh or the submesh doesn't exists.

entries.d: Returns the radius of the smallest sphere which can contain the mesh.
entries.r: Returns the radius the mesh.

entries.s: MeshVertex(x, y, z, u.f, v.f, Color [, NormalX, NormalY, NormalZ])
entries.d: Add a vertex to the current mesh previously created with CreateMesh. Specific attributes to the newly created vertex can be added with MeshVertexTangent. To create a new face use MeshFace.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Set color information to the current vertex previously added with MeshVertexPosition or MeshVertex. To have any effect, the material associated to the mesh has to be defined with SetMaterialColor(#Material, #PB_Material_AmbientColor, -1) and AmbientColor() set to a positive value. This function needs a vertex created before to apply color to it.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Return the number of vertices of the mesh.
entries.r: Returns the vertices number of the mesh, or zero if the mesh or the submesh doesn't exist.

entries.d: Set normal information to the current vertex previously added with MeshVertexPosition or MeshVertex. The normal vector is used to calculate lightning on an object. To automatically computes the vector normal once the mesh is created, use NormalizeMesh.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Add a new vertex to the current mesh previously created with CreateMesh. To set specific attributes to the newly created vertex, use the following commands: MeshVertexNormal, MeshVertexTangent, MeshVertexColor and MeshVertexTextureCoordinate. If several attributes needs to be specified, MeshVertex can be used instead. To create a new face use MeshFace.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Set tangent information to the current vertex previously added with MeshVertexPosition or MeshVertex. The tangent vector is mainly used in shader scripts. To automatically compute the tangent vector once the mesh is created, use BuildMeshTangents.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Set UVW information to the current vertex previously added with MeshVertexPosition or MeshVertex. The UVW information is used to apply the texture on the mesh.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Normalize the mesh or the submesh. It will automatically compute the normal vector for all vertices of the specified mesh or submesh. Dynamic meshes are not supported (meshes created with the #PB_Mesh_Dynamic flag).
entries.r: None

entries.d: Save the mesh. The saved mesh can be loaded back with the LoadMesh command.
entries.r: None

entries.s: Result = SetMeshData(#Mesh, SubMesh, DataArray(), Flags, FirstIndex, LastIndex)
entries.d: Set internal mesh data, like vertices, face etc. Dynamic meshes are not supported (meshes created with the #PB_Mesh_Dynamic flag).
entries.r: Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure.

entries.d: Set the mesh default material.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Returns the number of submeshes of the mesh.
entries.r: Returns the number of submeshes of the mesh.

entries.s: TransformMesh(#Mesh, x, y, z, ScaleX, ScaleY, ScaleZ, RotateX, RotateY, RotateZ [, SubMesh])
entries.d: Transform the Mesh according to the given parameters. Dynamic meshes are not supported for transform (meshes created with the #PB_Mesh_Dynamic flag).
entries.r: None

entries.d: Start the mesh update, to modify in real time its vertices and other values. The mesh has to be created with the #PB_Mesh_Dynamic flag. Once the mesh modifications are finished, FinishMesh needs to be called. The mesh can use the following commands to change their properties: MeshIndex, MeshFace, MeshVertexPosition, MeshVertexNormal, MeshVertexTangent, MeshVertexColor and MeshVertexTextureCoordinate.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Update the bounding box of the mesh. If a mesh has been manually modified, its bounding box has to be recalculated, especially if the mesh is used for collisions. The bounding box is the smallest box which can contain the whole mesh.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Updates the mouse state. This function should be used before MouseDeltaX, MouseDeltaY, MouseX, MouseY or MouseButton.
entries.r: Nonzero if the mouse state has been updated, zero otherwise.

entries.d: Initializes the mouse environment for later use. You should call this function before any other functions in this library. If the result is zero, no mouse is available.
entries.r: Nonzero if the mouse functions are available, zero otherwise. This function tries to open DirectX (v3.0 with NT4.0 compatibility or v7.0 otherwise); if it fails then DirectX is either not available or is too old to be used.

entries.d: Returns zero if the specified button number is not pressed, otherwise the button is pressed. Any number of buttons can be pressed at the same time. ExamineMouse must be called before this function to update the actual button's state.
entries.r: Nonzero if the specified mouse button is pressed, zero otherwise.

entries.d: Returns the mouse 'x' movement (in pixels) since the last call of this function.
entries.r: The mouse 'x' movement (in pixels) since the last call of this function. It can be either a negative or positive value, depending on whether or not the mouse has been moved to the left or the right since the last call. ExamineMouse should be called before this function to update the actual mouse position.

entries.d: Returns the mouse 'y' movement (in pixels) since the last call of this function.
entries.r: The mouse 'y' movement (in pixels) since the last call of this function. It can be either a negative or positive value, depending on whether or not the mouse has been moved up or down since the last call. ExamineMouse should be called before this function to update the actual mouse position.

entries.d: Changes the absolute position (in pixels) of the mouse in the current screen. This is useful when using MouseX or MouseY.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Returns the number of ticks the mouse wheel has moved since the last function call. ExamineMouse should be called before this function to update the mouse status.
entries.r: The number of ticks the mouse wheel has moved since the last function call. The value is positive if the wheel has moved forward and negative if the wheel has moved backwards.

entries.d: Returns the actual mouse 'x' position (in pixels) on the current screen. The position can be changed easily with the MouseLocate function. ExamineMouse should be called before this function to update the actual mouse position.
entries.r: The actual mouse 'x' position (in pixels) on the current screen.

entries.d: Returns the actual mouse 'y' position (in pixels) on the current screen. The position can be changed easily with the MouseLocate function. ExamineMouse should be called before this function to update the actual mouse position.
entries.r: The actual mouse 'y' position (in pixels) on the current screen.

entries.d: Locks or releases the mouse to allow its use under standard OS. This is typically called after checking the result of IsScreenActive function.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Frees the specified movie and all its resources.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Initialize the movie environment for later use. You must call this function before any other functions in this library.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if initialization was successful. If zero is returned then the movie library cannot be used.

entries.d: Tests if the given #Movie number is a valid and correctly initialized movie.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if #Movie is a valid movie and zero otherwise.

entries.d: Loads the specified movie file and prepares it for playback.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the movie was loaded correctly and zero if loading the movie failed (format not supported or file not found). If #PB_Any was used for the #Movie parameter then the generated number is returned on success.

entries.d: Control the audio stream of a movie. Volume and balance can be modified during playback. Changes occur immediately.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Returns the height of the movie.
entries.r: Returns the height of the movie in pixels. If the result equals -1, then no video stream is found (or isn't compatible), however the audio stream can still be played.

entries.d: Returns additional information about the movie.
entries.r: Returns the value specified in the 'Flags' parameter.

entries.d: Returns the length of the movie.
entries.r: Returns the length of the movie in frames.

entries.d: Change the movie's playback position to the given frame.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Get the playback status of the movie.
entries.r: Returns one of the following values: -1: Movie is paused. 0: Movie is stopped > 0: Movie is playing. The returned value is the current frame number displayed.

entries.d: Returns the width of the movie.
entries.r: Returns the width of the movie in pixels. If the result equals -1, then no video stream is found (or isn't compatible), however the audio stream can still be played.

entries.d: Pauses the movie playback. Playback can be resumed using the ResumeMovie function.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Start to play a movie previously loaded with LoadMovie on the specified window.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the movie started playing correctly and zero if there was an error.

entries.d: Resize and move the movie display area on the movie window.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Continue to play the movie, after a PauseMovie call.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Stop playing the movie. If the movie is played again, it will restart from the beginning.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Loads the specified music from the specified memory buffer. PlayMusic can be used to start playing the music. ModPlug supports a lot of music formats, which includes: Protracker (4 channels), FastTracker (up to 32 channels, 16-bit quality), Impulse Tracker, etc.
entries.r: Nonzero if the music module has been successfully loaded, zero otherwise.

entries.d: Stop and remove the specified music previously loaded with the LoadMusic or CatchMusic functions from memory. Once a music has been freed, it can't be played anymore.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Returns the current pattern position of the playing music module.
entries.r: The current pattern position of the playing music module. The first pattern position is zero.

entries.d: Returns the current row position in the pattern of the playing music module.
entries.r: The current row position of the playing music module. The first row position is zero.

entries.d: Tests if the given music module is valid and correctly initialized.
entries.r: Nonzero if the music module is valid, zero otherwise.

entries.d: Loads the specified music module. PlayMusic can be used to start playing the music. ModPlug supports a lot of music formats, which includes: Protracker (4 channels), FastTracker (up to 32 channels, 16-bit quality), Impulse Tracker, etc.
entries.r: Nonzero if the music module has been successfully loaded, zero otherwise.

entries.d: Change the master volume of the specified music, in real-time.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Starts to play the specified music previously loaded with the LoadMusic or CatchMusic functions.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Changes the current pattern position of the playing #Music to the new one.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Stop the #Music (if it was playing).
entries.r: None

entries.d: Close the specified connection.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Shutdown the specified running server. All clients connected to this server are automatically removed. The port is freed and can be reused.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Returns the unique system identifier of the connection.
entries.r: Returns the system identifier. This result is sometimes also known as 'Handle'. Look at the extra chapter Handles and Numbers for more information.

entries.d: Create a new network server on the local computer using the specified port. To support TLS encryption, UseNetworkTLS needs to be called before this command and a TLS flag needs to be specified.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the server was created successfully and zero if creation failed, for example, due to the port being already in use. If #PB_Any was used as the #Server parameter then the generated number is returned on success.

entries.d: This function returns the connection of the client that sent data and is only needed on the server side.
entries.r: Returns the connection of the client that caused the event.

entries.d: This function returns the number of the server which has received data, allowing multiple servers to be managed on one computer. It is only needed on the server side.
entries.r: Returns the #Server number of the server causing the event.

entries.d: Start examining the available IP addresses on the local computer. NextIPAddress is used to retrieve each IP.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if examining the addresses works and zero if it failed.

entries.d: Free an IPv6 address. This function only works with IPv6 addresses returned by MakeIPAddress, NextIPAddress and GetClientIP, and must not be used with IPv4 addresses.
entries.r: None

entries.d: This function returns the IP address of the client and should be called after EventClient(). If the connection is an IPv6 connection the returned address must be freed with FreeIP().
entries.r: Returns the IP address of the client.

entries.d: Returns the client port and should be called after EventClient.
entries.r: Returns the port of the client.

entries.d: Returns the computer's hostname.
entries.r: Returns the host name.

entries.d: Returns the given field value of the specified IP address.
entries.r: Returns the value of the specified field, in the range 0 to 255.

entries.d: Returns the string representation in dotted form (ie: "127.0.0.1" for IPv4 or "::1" for IPv6) of the specified numerical IPAddress.
entries.r: Returns the IP address as a string.

entries.s: Result = MakeIPAddress(Field0, Field1, Field2, Field3 [, Field4, Field5, Field6, Field7])
entries.d: Returns the equivalent numeric value of the specified IP address.
entries.r: Returns the IP address.

entries.d: Checks if an event happened on a network connection created with OpenNetworkConnection.
entries.r: Returns one of the following values: #PB_NetworkEvent_None : Nothing has happened #PB_NetworkEvent_Data : Raw data has been received (to be read with ReceiveNetworkData) #PB_NetworkEvent_Disconnect: The client has been disconnected (connection closed).

entries.d: Checks if an event happened on one of the open network servers.
entries.r: Returns one of the following values: #PB_NetworkEvent_None : Nothing has happened #PB_NetworkEvent_Connect : A new client has been connected to the server (not available with #PB_Network_UDP connections) #PB_NetworkEvent_Data : Raw data has been received (to be read with ReceiveNetworkData) #PB_NetworkEvent_Disconnect: A client has quit the server (disconnection). Its associated connection is automatically closed, CloseNetworkConnection must not be called for this client. (Not available with #PB_Network_UDP connections.)

entries.d: Returns the next IP address of the local machine. ExamineIPAddresses must be called before this command.
entries.r: Returns the next IP address in numerical form. If the result is 0 then there are no more IP addresses to be examined. If ExamineIPAddresses is called with the #PB_Network_IPv6 format, the returned IP needs to freed with FreeIP after use.

entries.s: Connection = OpenNetworkConnection(ServerName$, Port [, Flags [, TimeOut [, LocalIP$ [, LocalPort]]]])
entries.d: Opens a network connection to the specified server. To support TLS encryption, UseNetworkTLS needs to be called before this command and a TLS flag needs to be specified.
entries.r: Returns the connection identifier for the opened connection if the connection was established correctly. If there was an error the result is zero.

entries.d: Receives raw data from the specified client. This function can be used by both client and server applications and should be called only after having received a #PB_NetworkEvent_Data event.
entries.r: Returns the number of bytes received. If 'Result' is equal to DataBufferLength then more data is available to be read. If an error occurred on the connection (link broken, connection close by the server etc...) 'Result' will be -1.

entries.d: Sends raw data to the specified client. This function can be used by both client and server applications.
entries.r: Returns the number of bytes actually sent. If the number of bytes returned is not equal to the 'Length' parameter the receiving buffer of the user is probably full. If nothing could be sent then 'Result' will equal -1.

entries.d: Send a string to the specified client. This function can be used by both client and server applications.
entries.r: Returns the number of bytes sent.

entries.d: Returns the unique system identifier of the server.
entries.r: Returns the system identifier. This result is sometimes also known as 'Handle'. Look at the extra chapter Handles and Numbers for more information.

entries.d: Enable and configure TLS support for network library. This command must be called before using CreateNetworkServer or OpenNetworkConnection with the TLS flags.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Attaches an existing object to a node.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Creates a new node at the specified position.
entries.r: Nonzero if the node was successfully created, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used for the #Node parameter then the generated number is returned on success.

entries.d: Detaches a previously attached object from a node.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Frees the specified node created with CreateNode before. All its associated memory is released and this object can't be used anymore. The attached objects are not freed automatically, and can be re-used.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Tests if the given node is valid and correctly initialized.
entries.r: Nonzero if the node is valid, zero otherwise.

entries.d: Move the specified node.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Change the fixed yaw axis of the node. The default behaviour of a node is to yaw around its own Y axis.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Returns the unique system identifier of the node.
entries.r: Returns the unique system identifier of the node.

entries.s: NodeLookAt(#Node, x, y, z [, DirectionX, DirectionY, DirectionZ])
entries.d: The point (in world unit) that a node is facing. The position of the node is not changed.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Get the pitch of the node.
entries.r: The current pitch value of the node.

entries.d: Get the roll of the node.
entries.r: The current roll value of the node.

entries.d: Returns the 'x' position of the node in the world.
entries.r: The 'x' position of the node in the world.

entries.d: Returns the 'y' position of the node in the world.
entries.r: The 'y' position of the node in the world.

entries.d: Get the yaw of the node.
entries.r: The current yaw value of the node.

entries.d: Returns the 'z' position of the node in the world.
entries.r: The 'z' position of the node in the world.

entries.d: Rotates the node according to the specified x,y,z angle values.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Scales the node according to the specified x,y,z values. When using #PB_Relative mode, this is a factor based scale which means the node size will be multiplied with the given value to obtain the new size.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Add time to the specified #NodeAnimation.
entries.r: None

entries.s: Result = CreateNodeAnimation(#NodeAnimation, NodeID, Length, Interpolation, RotationInterpolation)
entries.d: Creates a new node animation of the specified length. A node animation doesn't exist physically in the 3D world, it is an virtual track to move a node (and its attached object) easily around the world.
entries.r: Returns zero if the #NodeAnimation can't be created. If #PB_Any is used as '#NodeAnimation' parameter, the new node animation number is returned.

entries.d: Create a new keyframe for the #NodeAnimation. A keyframe is a point in the world at a specified time. When the node animation will be played, it will follow every keyframe and thus moving from points to points. The move will be interpolated to respect the time constraint. For example, if the first keyframe is set at time 0, the second at time 1000 and the third at time 3000, going from the first keyframe to the second will takes 1000 milliseconds, and going from the second keyframe to the third will takes 2000 milliseconds. The overall animation will take 3000 milliseconds.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Frees a node animation and releases all its associated memory. This node animation must not be used (by using its number with the other functions in this library) after calling this function, unless you create it again.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Returns the #NodeAnimation keyframe pitch.
entries.r: Returns the current node animation keyframe pitch, or zero if the keyframe doesn't exists.

entries.d: Returns the #NodeAnimation keyframe roll.
entries.r: Returns the current node animation keyframe roll, or zero if the keyframe doesn't exists.

entries.d: Returns the #NodeAnimation keyframe time.
entries.r: Returns the node animation keyframe time (in milliseconds), or zero if the keyframe doesn't exists.

entries.d: Returns the #NodeAnimation keyframe 'x' position.
entries.r: Returns the node animation keyframe 'x' position in the world, or zero if the keyframe doesn't exists.

entries.d: Returns the #NodeAnimation keyframe 'y' position.
entries.r: Returns the node animation keyframe 'y' position in the world, or zero if the keyframe doesn't exists.

entries.d: Returns the #NodeAnimation keyframe yaw.
entries.r: Returns the current node animation keyframe yaw, or zero if the keyframe doesn't exists.

entries.d: Returns the #NodeAnimation keyframe 'z' position.
entries.r: Returns the node animation keyframe 'z' position in the world, or zero if the keyframe doesn't exists.

entries.d: Returns the #NodeAnimation length.
entries.r: The node animation length (in milliseconds).

entries.d: Returns the current #NodeAnimation time.
entries.r: The current node animation time (in milliseconds) or 0 if the animation isn't running.

entries.d: Returns the #NodeAnimation weight. The weight is useful when playing several animations at once. For example to do a smooth transition from one animation to another, it is possible to reduce progressively the weight of the first animation and increase the weight of the second animation.
entries.r: The current node animation weight (value between 0.0 and 1.0). If the weight is 0, then the animation has no effect. If the weight is 1, then animation is fully playing.

entries.d: Return the specified #NodeAnimation status.
entries.r: The return value can be one of the following constants: #PB_NodeAnimation_Stopped: The animation is stopped (or has ended). #PB_NodeAnimation_Started: The animation is running.

entries.d: Changes the keyframe position for the #NodeAnimation.
entries.r: None

entries.s: SetNodeAnimationKeyFrameRotation(#NodeAnimation, KeyFrame, x, y, z [, w, Mode])
entries.d: Changes the keyframe rotation for the #NodeAnimation.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Changes the keyframe scale factor for the #NodeAnimation. The scale factor will be applied to the node associated to the animation.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Change the #NodeAnimation length.
Changes the current #NodeAnimation time. This is an absolute time position. To change the time relative to the current time, use AddNodeAnimationTime.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Changes the #NodeAnimation weight. The weight is useful when playing several animations at once. For example to do a smooth transition from one animation to another, it is possible to reduce progressively the weight of the first animation and increase the weight of the second animation.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Start the specified #NodeAnimation. The animation is always started from the beginning.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Stop the specified #NodeAnimation.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Returns the memory address of the assembly instruction that caused the current error. This command only returns a meaningful value if there was an error handled by OnErrorCall or OnErrorGoto.
entries.r: The memory address of the assembly instruction that caused the current error.

entries.d: Returns the error code of the currently handled error. This command only returns a meaningful value if there was an error handled by OnErrorCall or OnErrorGoto.
entries.r: One of the following values: #PB_OnError_InvalidMemory : Read or write operation on an invalid location #PB_OnError_Floatingpoint : Floating-point error #PB_OnError_Breakpoint : Debugger breakpoint reached (non-PureBasic breakpoints) #PB_OnError_IllegalInstruction : Attempt to execute an illegal instruction #PB_OnError_PriviledgedInstruction: Attempt to execute a privileged (system-) instruction #PB_OnError_DivideByZero : Division by zero (Windows only) Linux and Mac OSX report #PB_OnError_Floatingpoint for division by zero errors. In addition, every OS may have more possible error values. On Windows, custom errors can be raised with the RaiseError command.

entries.d: Returns the filename of the source code or includefile where the current error occurred. This command only returns a meaningful value if there was an error handled by OnErrorCall or OnErrorGoto. The tracking of line numbers needs to be enabled on compilation for this command to return the actual file name. To enable this feature, enable the "Enable OnError lines support" checkbox in the compiler options or specify the /LINENUMBERING (Windows) or --linenumbering (Linux, Mac OSX) command-line switch when compiling from the command-line.
entries.r: The filename of the error, or "OnError line support disabled" if the OnError lines support is disabled. (A simple way to check if the OnError lines support is enabled is to check if the result of ErrorLine is not -1.)

entries.d: Returns the line number in the source code where the current error occurred. This command only returns a meaningful value if there was an error handled by OnErrorCall or OnErrorGoto. The tracking of line numbers needs to be enabled on compilation for this command to return the actual line number. To enable this feature, enable the "Enable OnError lines support" checkbox in the compiler options or specify the /LINENUMBERING (Windows) or --linenumbering (Linux, Mac OSX) command-line switch when compiling from the command-line.
entries.r: The line number of the error, or -1 if the OnError lines support is disabled.

entries.d: Returns an error-message for the given error code in english.
entries.r: The message for the currently handled error. If the 'ErrorCode' parameter is set, an english error-message for this specific error will be returned.

entries.d: Returns the content of the specified CPU register at the time of the error. This command only returns a meaningful value if there was an error handled by OnErrorCall or OnErrorGoto.
entries.r: The content of the specified CPU register at the time of the error.

entries.d: After an error with the code #PB_OnError_InvalidMemory, this command returns the memory address which was read/written when the error occurred. This command has no meaning for other error codes.
entries.r: The memory address which was read/written when the error occurred, after a #PB_OnError_InvalidMemory error.

entries.d: Initializes the disassembling at the given address or address range. Important: The disassembly commands use the Udis86 disassembler library to decode the instructions. This library is released under the BSD license which can be viewed here. If ExamineAssembly and the related commands are used in a program that is to be made public, the above linked licence text must be included with the software.
entries.r: Nonzero if disassembling is possible, zero otherwise.

entries.d: Returns the address of the instruction that was disassembled by a call to NextInstruction.
entries.r: The address of the instruction that was disassembled by a call to NextInstruction.

entries.d: Returns a string representation of the instruction that was disassembled by a call to NextInstruction.
entries.r: A string representation of the instruction that was disassembled by a call to NextInstruction.

entries.d: Disassembles the next instruction after a call to ExamineAssembly. Information about the disassembled instruction can be read with InstructionString and InstructionAddress.
entries.r: Nonzero if the instruction was successfully disassembled, zero otherwise ('*EndAddress' that was specified in ExamineAssembly was reached).

entries.d: Changes the action taken if an error occurs to call the specified handler procedure. The handler can display information about the error to the user using the commands of this library and do any needed cleanup to shutdown the application. The program will end as soon as the handler returns.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Changes the action taken when an error occurs back to the system default. This usually means displaying an error dialog and exiting the program, but it may also mean to just ignore certain errors. To exit the program on every error, use OnErrorExit.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Changes the action taken if an error occurs to directly exit the program, even if the default action on the system is not to exit the program on this kind of error. The system may display an error dialog or print an error-message on the console on exit.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Changes the action taken when an error occurs to jump to the specified label address and continue program execution there. After the jump to the label, the functions of this library can be used to get further information about the error.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Artificially create the given error. The appropriate error action will be taken (call of the error handler or program termination by the system if no handler is set). The ErrorNumber will be available inside the error handler with the ErrorCode command.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Add a new empty directory to the specified pack previously created with CreatePack.
entries.r: Nonzero if the empty directory has been successfully added to the packfile.

entries.d: Add and compress the file to the specified pack previously created with CreatePack. Adding a large file can take a long time. PackerCallback can be used to monitor or abort the compression.
entries.r: Nonzero if the file has been successfully added to the packfile. If the file can't be compressed, it will be stored as is in the packfile.

entries.d: Add and compress the memory buffer to the specified pack previously created with CreatePack. PackerCallback can be used to monitor or abort the compression.
entries.r: Nonzero if the buffer has been successfully added to the packfile. If the memory buffer can't be compressed, it will be stored as is in the packfile.

entries.d: Open a previously existing pack file from memory. Before opening a pack file, at least one packer has to be registered with one of the following command: UseZipPacker, UseLzmaPacker, UseTarPacker, UseBriefLZPacker. Once opened, the pack content can be listed with ExaminePack.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the pack file has been successfully opened, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used as the #Pack parameter then the generated pack number is returned.

entries.d: Close the specified pack file.
entries.r: None

entries.s: Result = CompressMemory(*Buffer, Size, *Output, OutputSize [, Plugin [, Level]])
entries.d: Compress the buffer content into the output buffer. The output buffer length needs to be at least as long as the buffer to compress. PackerCallback can be used to monitor or abort the compression.
entries.r: Return the compressed size if the buffer has been successfully compressed, zero otherwise. If the buffer data can't be compressed (already compressed data generally don't compress anymore), it will return zero.

entries.d: Create a new empty pack file. If the file already exists, it will be replaced with a new empty file. Before creating a pack file, at least one packer has to be registered with one of the following command: UseZipPacker, UseBriefLZPacker.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the pack file has been successfully created, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used as the #Pack parameter then the generated pack number is returned.

entries.d: Start to examine the pack content. NextPackEntry has to be called to list the entries found in the pack file. The pack has to be previously opened with OpenPack or CatchPack. Packs being created with CreatePack can not be examined.
entries.r: Nonzero if the pack can be examined, zero otherwise.

entries.d: Tests if the given pack number is a valid and correctly initialized pack.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if #Pack is a valid pack and zero if not.

entries.d: Go to the next entry in the pack file. ExaminePack has to be called before calling this command. To get more information about the current entry, use PackEntrySize, PackEntryType and PackEntryName. To uncompress the current entry, use UncompressPackMemory or UncompressPackFile.
entries.r: Nonzero if the pack contain another entry, zero otherwise.

entries.d: Open a previously existing pack file. Before opening a pack file, at least one packer has to be registered with one of the following command: UseZipPacker, UseLzmaPacker, UseTarPacker, UseBriefLZPacker. Once opened, the pack content can be listed with ExaminePack.
entries.r: Returns nonzero if the pack file has been successfully opened, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used as the #Pack parameter then the generated pack number is returned.

entries.d: Returns the file date of the current pack entry, set with NextPackEntry.
entries.r: Returns the file date or -1 if no date is available.

entries.d: Returns the name of the current entry, set with NextPackEntry.
entries.r: Returns the name of the current entry.

entries.d: Returns the size of the current entry, set with NextPackEntry.
entries.r: Returns the size of the current entry.

entries.d: Returns the type of the current entry, set with NextPackEntry.
entries.r: Returns one of the following values: #PB_Packer_File : the current entry is a file #PB_Packer_Directory: the current entry is a directory

entries.d: Set a callback to monitor or abort the compression for CompressMemory, AddPackFile and AddPackMemory. The callback will be called at regular intervalls during the compression process.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Uncompress the buffer content into the output buffer. The output buffer length needs to be at least as long as the buffer to uncompress.
entries.r: Return the uncompressed size if the buffer has been successfully uncompressed, -1 otherwise.

entries.d: Uncompress into the specified filename from the current pack entry being examined with ExaminePack and NextPackEntry. If the filename already exists, it will erased and replaced with the new uncompressed data.
entries.r: Return the uncompressed size if the pack entry has been successfully uncompressed into the filename, -1 otherwise.

entries.d: Uncompress into the memory buffer from the current pack entry being examined with ExaminePack and NextPackEntry.
entries.r: Return the uncompressed size if the pack entry has been successfully uncompressed into the memory buffer, -1 otherwise.

entries.d: Enable BriefLZ compress, uncompress and archive support to the packer library. The created archives are a custom format created for PureBasic. BriefLZ compression is very fast and the packer is very small, it could be the right choice for program which needs a small executable size. Uncompress is also very fast, but compress ratio is not as good as Zip or Lzma.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Enable Jcalg1 uncompress support to the packer library. This is an old algorithm which was used in previous version of PureBasic, so it is still available to allow to support old compressed files. Compression and archive support is no more available. This packer is only available on Windows x86 (32-bit). This packer is deprecated and no more supported.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Enable Lzma compress, uncompress and 7z archive support to the packer library. Lzma compression is considered as one of the best available multipurpose compression algorithm. It provides very good compress ratio and fast uncompress. Compressing can be slow. For more information: Wikipedia - Lzma.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Enable Tar compress, uncompress and Tar archive support to the packer library. Bzip2 and Gzip compression are both supported. Compressing and uncompressing Tar archives are usually fast.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Enable Zip compress, uncompress and archive support to the packer library. The created pack will be compatible with other Zip archives in 2.0 format. The created archive size can be up to 2GB. For more information: Wikipedia - Zip.
entries.r: None

entries.s: Result = CreateParticleEmitter(#ParticleEmitter, Width, Height, Depth, Type, [, x.f, y.f, z.f])
entries.d: Creates a new empty particle emitter of the given size.
entries.r: Nonzero if the particle emitter has been successfully created, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used as #ParticleEmitter parameter then the auto-generated number of the new particle emitter will be returned.

entries.d: Enables or disables the particle emitter. When disabled, no more particle are emitted.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Frees the particle emitter. All its associated memory is released and this object can't be used anymore.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Gets a particle emitter defined in an OGRE script file.
entries.r: Zero if the particle emitter isn't found or can't be loaded from script files. If #PB_Any is used as '#ParticleEmitter' parameter, the new particle emitter number is returned.

entries.d: Hides or shows the specified particle emitter.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Tests if the given particle emitter is valid and correctly initialized.
entries.r: Nonzero if the particle emitter is valid, zero otherwise.

entries.d: Move the specified particle emitter.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Changes the particles acceleration vector. It can be useful to simulate gravity, wind, etc.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Changes the particle angle when emitted.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Changes the particles color fader rate.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Changes the particles color range for the particle emitter. Every emitted particle will get a random value, within the 'StartColor' and 'EndColor' range (gradient between these two color).
entries.r: None

entries.d: Changes the #ParticleEmitter emission rate.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Changes the emitted particle angles. All particules will have the same angle.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Changes the direction of the particle emitter according to the specified x,y,z values.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Returns the unique system identifier of the particle emitter.
entries.r: The unique system identifier of the particle emitter.

entries.d: Returns the particle emitter 'x' position in the world.
entries.r: The particle emitter 'x' position in the world (according to the given 'Mode').

entries.d: Returns the particle emitter 'y' position in the world.
entries.r: The particle emitter 'y' position in the world (according to the given 'Mode').

entries.d: Returns the particle emitter 'z' position in the world.
entries.r: The particle emitter 'z' position in the world (according to the given 'Mode').

entries.d: Assigns a material to the specified particle emitter. This material will be used by all the particles of this emitter. An emitter can only have one material assigned at once.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Changes the current particle emitter scale rate.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Change the particles dimensions. Particles are 2D planes (billboards) which always face the camera. All particles in an emitter always have the same size.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Changes the current particle emitter speed factor.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Change the particles time to live for the particle emitter. Every particle will live at least 'MinimumTime' and at most the 'MaximumTime' (in world time unit). A random value, within this range, will be used by every particle emitted.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Changes the particles velocity.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Resizes the particle emitter to the new specified 'Width', 'Height' and 'Depth' dimension.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Closes a preference file previously opened with OpenPreferences or created with CreatePreferences.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Creates a new empty preference file. If the file already exists, the file is erased.
entries.r: Nonzero if the file has been successfully created, zero otherwise.

entries.d: Starts the enumeration of all the groups found in the current preference file. NextPreferenceGroup can be used to list all the group found.
entries.r: Nonzero if the enumeration has been successfully started, zero otherwise.

entries.d: Starts the enumeration of all the keys found in the current group of the preference file. The current group can be selected with PreferenceGroup or by examining all groups with ExaminePreferenceGroups. NextPreferenceKey can be used to list all the keys found.
entries.r: Nonzero if the enumeration has been successfully started, zero otherwise.

entries.d: Ensures that all preferences changes are written to disk.
entries.r: Nonzero if the preferences has been successfully written the disk. If an error occurred (ie: disk full, disk error), it will return zero.

entries.d: Retrieves information about the next group found in the enumeration started with ExaminePreferenceGroups. To get the name of the group, use PreferenceGroupName. The current examined preference group will also be used when values are read from the preferences or when the keys are examined with ExaminePreferenceKeys.
entries.r: Nonzero if more groups are available in the current enumeration, zero otherwise.

entries.d: Retrieves information about the next key found in the enumeration started with ExaminePreferenceKeys. To get the name and the value of the key, use PreferenceKeyName and PreferenceKeyValue.
entries.r: Nonzero if more keys are available in the current enumeration, zero otherwise.

entries.d: Opens a previously existing preference file.
entries.r: Nonzero if the file has been successfully opened, zero otherwise.

entries.d: Writes a new comment line in the current preference file.
entries.r: None

entries.d: Creates a new group (in the form: [Name$]) or changes the current group in the preference file. All following read or write operations will be restricted to this group. To move outside of any groups, an empty 'Name$' can be used.
entries.r: Nonzero if the group was already created, zero otherwise.

entries.d: Returns the name of the current group being enumerated with ExaminePreferenceGroups or previously selected with PreferenceGroup.
entries.r: The name of the current group being enumerated with ExaminePreferenceGroups or previously selected with PreferenceGroup.

entries.d: Returns the name of the current key being enumerated with ExaminePreferenceKeys. To get the value of the key, use PreferenceKeyValue.
entries.r: The name of the current key being enumerated with ExaminePreferenceKeys.

entries.d: Returns the value, in string form, of the current key being enumerated with ExaminePreferenceKeys. To get the name of the key, use PreferenceKeyName.
entries.r: The value, in string form, of the current key being enumerated with ExaminePreferenceKeys.

entries.d: Try to read the specified associated 'Key$' value.
entries.r: The value associated to the specified key, as a double number. if the key isn't found the default value is returned.

entries.d: Try to read the specified associated 'Key$' value.
entries.r: The value associated to the specified key, as a float number. if the key isn't found the default value is returned.

entries.d: Try to read the specified associated 'Key$' value.
entries.r: The value associated to the specified key, as an integer number. if the key isn't found the default value is returned.

entries.d: Try to read the specified associated 'Key$' value.
entries.r: The value associated to the specified key, as a long number. if the key isn't found the default value is returned.

entries.d: Try to read the specified associated 'Key$' value.
entries.r: The value associated to the specified key, as a quad number. if the key isn't found the default value is returned.

entries.d: Try to read the specified associated 'Key$' value.
entries.r: The value associated to the specified key, as a string. if the key isn't found the default value is returned.

entries.d: Removes the specified 'Group$' and all its keys.

entries.d: Removes the specified key and its value.

entries.d: Creates or changes the specified key and its associated double value under the form: 'Key$ = Value' in the preference file, previously created with CreatePreferences or opened with OpenPreferences.
